response.name: list_projects
response.description: List all Quire research projects. Each has a stable slug (use it as the project id elsewhere), name, description and counts of documents, notes and sources.

response.name: list_project_files
response.description: List a research project's documents (papers carry authors, year, arXiv id, DOI, source URL and an abstract snippet), notes and web sources, each with a stable id.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

response.name: get_file
response.description: Read a research document. By default returns its text page by page ("--- Page N ---" markers, up to 20,000 characters of page text per call; pass `pages` to continue) and flags pages that are mostly figures, contain embedded images or are heavy on formulas. Use get_page_images to see figures, tables, formulas or scans. format="pdf"/"original" returns the raw file as an embedded binary resource, which only Claude Code can open; use it only when the user needs the file itself.

pages.description: pages to read, e.g. "1-10", "3,7" or "20-"; default: from page 1

format.description: text (default) = extracted page text; pdf/original = raw binary; markdown = body

response.name: get_page_images
response.description: Render pages of a research document's PDF as JPEG images (max 4 per call) to see figures, tables, formulas or scanned pages.

response.name: get_note
response.description: Read a research project's note as Markdown.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

response.name: upload_markdown
response.description: WRITES to Quire: creates a new Markdown note (section="notes", the default) or Markdown document (section="documents") in a research project, optionally inside an existing folder. Never edits or deletes. Re-sending the same title and text returns the existing item instead of a copy; note titles are unique per project. Max 512 KB. For Markdown you write yourself; to upload an existing .md file use create_upload_link.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

markdown.description: the Markdown text; a leading "# Title" line is used as the title if none is given

folder.description: existing folder name or id in that section; default: top level

response.name: upload_pdf
response.description: WRITES to Quire: downloads a PDF from a public https URL (the server fetches it, max 50 MB) into a research project's Documents. Public https URL only (no logins, no private or local addresses; pass the direct PDF link, e.g. https://arxiv.org/pdf/<id>); for a local file use create_upload_link. The same PDF already in the project is returned instead of a copy. Large PDFs may return status "processing"; calling again is safe. Never edits or deletes.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

url.description: public https link to the PDF

title.description: 1-200 characters; default: taken from the PDF

folder.description: existing Documents folder name or id; default: top level

response.name: add_paper
response.description: WRITES to Quire: adds a paper to a research project from an arXiv id or URL (e.g. "2401.01234", arxiv.org/abs/...) or a DOI, with its title, authors, year and abstract, and the PDF when one can be fetched (otherwise a metadata-only record). The same arXiv paper (any version) or DOI already in the project is returned instead of a copy. A plain URL is not accepted: use upload_pdf. Never edits or deletes.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

reference.description: arXiv id or URL, or a DOI

folder.description: existing Documents folder name or id; default: top level

response.name: create_upload_link
response.description: WRITES to Quire (via the link): creates a one-time upload URL (valid 10 minutes, single use) for an EXISTING local file, .pdf into a research project's Documents or .md into its Notes or Documents. The file bytes never pass through this tool: run the returned curl (PUT) on the machine that has the file, then check get_upload_status. The same file uploaded again returns the existing item. Never edits or deletes.

project.description: research project slug or id, from list_projects

section.description: documents (PDF or Markdown) or notes (Markdown only)

filename.description: name of the local file, ending in .pdf, .md or .markdown

folder.description: existing folder name or id in that section; default: top level

response.name: get_upload_status
response.description: Report what an upload link produced: pending (not used yet), processing, created, duplicate, failed or expired, with the new file or note id once done.
